newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian court halts Purneftegaz switch to Sidanko.
newsitem.headline: Russian court halts Purneftegaz switch to Sidanko.

text.p: An arbitration court has placed an injunction on the transfer of oil producer Purneftegaz from state-controlled NK Rosneft to NK Sidanko while ownership is in dispute, a Rosneft spokesman said on Friday.
A Moscow court in November recognised a claim by NK Sidanko to a 38 percent stake, equivalent to 50.7 percent of the voting shares, in AO Rosneft-Purneftegaz but the dispute has continued.
It is unclear how the ruling will affect a tender for 51 percent of Sidanko, bids for which are being accepted until January 9.

The Federal Property Fund, which is organising the auction, had listed the Purneftegaz stake among Sidanko assets when it announced the Sidanko auction on December 10 and said the starting price for the Sidanko stake would be $129 million.
Sidanko shareholders will hold an extraordinary meeting on December 28 at which they will discuss questions relating to the issue of shares, a company spokesman told Reuters on Friday.
But he declined to give details except to say that questions of the ownership of Purnefetegaz would not be discussed.
Sidanko is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating units are Chernogorneft, Kondpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz.
